title: The story of Moses at the burning bush is one of the most honest leadership moments in the Bible.
paragraphs: The story of Moses at the burning bush is one of the most honest leadership moments in the Bible.
God called him to confront Pharaoh, lead Israel out of slavery, and carry one of the greatest missions in history.
And Moses… hesitated.

He didn’t step forward with confidence.
He stepped back with questions.
“Who am I?”
“What if they don’t believe me?”
“I’m not good with words.”
“Please send someone else.”

Moses wasn’t lazy.
He wasn’t rebellious.
He was aware of his limitations.
And sometimes that awareness can make a calling feel terrifying.
Many people imagine that the heroes of Scripture were fearless.
But Moses reminds us that even the greatest leaders sometimes begin with reluctance.
What changed Moses wasn’t a sudden boost of confidence.
God never told Moses, “You’re actually more capable than you think.”
Instead, God kept repeating something deeper:
“I will be with you.”
That sentence changes everything.
Because the power of the calling was never going to come from Moses.
It would come from God.
One of the most overlooked truths in Scripture is this:
God rarely calls people who feel fully prepared.
He calls people who must depend on Him.
He calls shepherds who feel forgotten.
He calls fishermen who feel ordinary.
He calls reluctant leaders standing in front of burning bushes.
And sometimes the hesitation you feel isn’t proof that you’re unqualified.
It’s proof that you understand the weight of the assignment.
Moses eventually obeyed.
And the reluctant shepherd became the man who stood before Pharaoh, parted the Red Sea, and led a nation through the wilderness.
Not because he believed in himself.
But because he believed God would be with him.
And sometimes that’s the only qualification you need.
